provenance.registrations: TaskCreate consumes canonical 24-byte TaskDesc records; ModeRequest consumes canonical 16-byte Mode records. Callback tuples and ASCII names identify regional registrations. EU Monsgage callbacks are explicitly exposed within existing opaque native code. Message face/wait tasks form a real three-record array. Only absent EU link-exchange tasks omit records; work-size and callback differences use field-level guards.
provenance.names: Each bounded ASCII name is directly referenced by one or more verified registration records. Shared name addresses have one C owner. String bounds end at their first NUL.
provenance.task_descriptor_owners: The 108 individual task descriptors have independent address-taking consumers without cross-record indexing. Callback ownership, name ownership, and text, rodata and descriptor group ordering agree across US, JP and EU. Each callback translation unit emits one ordinary data section in the original order.
provenance.pooh_animation: mode_sio2.c func_080C7FEC has explicit action cases and direction helpers: C7CC8/C7D60 select 0..4, C7DF8 selects 0..7, C7E98 selects 0..1, and C7F18 selects 1/3. The canonical 4048[][5] row stride and C7CC8 row0..4 prove 5x5 records; the direction lookup normal outputs cover columns0..4 and its sentinel preserves the cached direction selection. Single-action branches become scalar objects. The fifth physical3FF8 record is a separate neutral scalar4038, not an asserted used array entry. All scalar bytes and complete record layouts match across US/JP/EU.
provenance.poo_native_data: All 51 Pooh task descriptors directly reference callbacks in poo.c. The three 144-entry const-u16-pointer indexes feed task_poo_map_0 and func_080CA36C and remain shared with three event-background records through poo_background_data.h. The five 16-byte butterfly records are AnimDef metadata selected by func_080D1FB8 and read by func_080D2034. In US, JP and EU the descriptors, background indexes and butterfly table form one uninterrupted initialized-data run in callback-family order. Ordinary definitions in poo.c reproduce its entire 0xBD8-byte range, every object offset and all relocations. The butterfly table uses native mutable storage, consistent with this data run; its consumer retains a const view. The former custom readonly placement did not establish original const qualification. Lower motion, point, cabbage and name placements are unchanged pending separate source-boundary evidence.
provenance.world_logo_owner: The nine world-logo selector and task callbacks form a separate final code run in mode_sio.c. Their two private selector tables, two registration records and two aligned names form complete native data and rodata groups across US, JP and EU. The 13-entry world-name and logo-ID bounds come from the selector wrap logic. Native alignment supplies the three bytes after the logo-ID array and the one byte between names.
provenance.sio_menu_owner: All remaining SIO mode descriptors reference callbacks in mode_sio.c, and its world-menu, level-offset and card-trade navigation tables are referenced only by those callbacks and helpers. Six descriptors and four tables form one complete native initialized-data run in US/JP; EU omits the two card-trade descriptors and their navigation table. Original ROM order, object extents, relocations and contents remain independently checked. The separate name sections include intervening UI data and are not merged.
provenance.mode_tail_ownership: Deck/menu, Continue and Event callback groups each reproduce their native code, name, initialized-data and BSS runs in all three original ROMs. The shared event ID is unsigned as established by the original message-handler switch branches.
provenance.bos6_native_data: The 96-entry PcSpriteCmd pointer index and 14-entry PcAnimStep pointer index are consumed only by bos6.c animation selection and command execution. The two-entry shake index is consumed only by its Pc field-shake helper. In all three original ROMs these three indexes and five TaskDesc records form an uninterrupted 0x238-byte initialized-data run in the same order: sprite index, animation index, Pc registration, shake index, PcFld/PcFlt/PcAcd/BosLst registrations. Each registration directly references callbacks in bos6.c. Ordinary definitions reproduce every original address, byte and relocation without section attributes. The lower-ROM command, animation, palette, shot and name groups retain their existing organization; this consolidation does not claim additional original source boundaries.
provenance.backupstat_owner: The mode lifecycle and state editor are the only users of the status-name index, six-entry BackupStatEntry table and diagnostic labels. The same Shift-JIS bytes occur in every region. Ordinary string literals produce the original deferred reverse initializer order; a const metadata table, const reader and native mode name reproduce the complete 0xD0-byte readonly run, including normal four-byte literal alignment. The original 0x1C-byte initialized-data run remains unchanged. The obsolete storage TU, private declarations and fixed-address text aliases are removed without changing text contents or code.
provenance.status_owner: The twelve status UI task descriptors and their six EU-only language indexes retain their original native initialized-data owner. The following Boogie descriptor belongs to boss_boogie.c with its lifecycle callbacks and private work pointer; every original descriptor/index object address, extent and content contract is preserved.
provenance.pooh_eu_background_indexes: The EU-only five-language floor-background pointer indexes are consumed only by poo.c func_080D313C, which selects the appropriate floor span and copies it to background VRAM. Their ten pointers immediately follow that owner's established native initialized-data run. Ordinary EU-scoped definitions extend the run from 0xBD8 to 0xC00 without changing payloads, pointer targets or any US/JP definition. Both original index object contracts and all preceding Pooh object contracts remain validated.
provenance.lst_staffroll_owners: The StaffRoll helpers beginning at func_081125BC and its three lifecycle callbacks share one exclusively referenced work pointer, its mode descriptor and diagnostic name. Their code, native data/rodata and RAM runs reproduce the original order across all regions without code changes or added alignment. They now live in mode_staffroll.c; existing StaffRoll types move to its header. The preceding Lst callbacks, eight task descriptors, four-entry LstAnimSet and shake-pointer index remain in bos7.c. The index retains its const pointer-array type and uses ordinary rodata; the animation records and descriptors form the immediately following native 0xE0-byte data run. Each table is consumed only by that owner. The separate staff-roll script/text catalogs and lower boss data/name groups remain unchanged.
provenance.boogie_ursula_native_data: The nine Boogie and nine Ursula TaskDesc records all point to callbacks in bos4.c. The four 12-entry Ursula background-map indexes are repeatedly selected and compared by object address in func_080DB978 and task_bos_ursula_2, with SetBgMapBlocks explicitly using a 4-by-3 grid. These tables and descriptors form one uninterrupted native 0x270-byte initialized-data run in all three original ROMs: nine Boogie registrations, four map indexes, nine Ursula registrations. Ordinary definitions in the code owner preserve each original object, all relocations and every code byte. The storage-only boss_ursula_data TU and its private declaration header are removed. Later MapChk and other ROM placements remain unchanged; this batch does not assert a new code boundary.
provenance.bos5_native_data: Six boss TaskDesc records, the world-selection palette cycle and its Mode record form a complete initialized-data run in bos5.c, with four additional five-language pointer indexes between the sixth task record and palette cycle in EU. Every descriptor uses callbacks in that source, and palette and language indexes have repeated code or MdModel consumers there. Ordinary definitions preserve all original object extents and callbacks: 0x118 bytes in US/JP and 0x168 bytes in EU. The former worldselect_data storage TU and private header are removed. The separate lower-ROM name, actor and model data retain their existing organization.
provenance.title_readonly_owner: The four title task names and two readonly lookup tables share title.c consumers. The menu loops enumerate four s32 entries {4,5,1,2}; the luminance callback copies exactly three s16 entries {-7,0,3} into its local array. Ordinary const definitions reproduce the complete 0x5E-byte readonly run in every original region with native alignment, preserving all four original name extents and both independently bounded table spans. The old raw fragments and address aliases are removed without code or asset-payload changes.
provenance.mode_allmap_readonly_owner: The all-map mode copies the complete existing AllmapRoomOrder and AllmapRoomDirs records into locals. The four-direction loop builds a mask in0..15 for the sixteen-entry order and reads the four-entry direction permutation. Both definitions have only mode_allmap.c consumers. Ordinary const definitions follow the existing mode name in one native0x5C-byte readonly section in all regions, replacing the exact80-byte raw metadata fragment. provenance.allmap_readonly_suffix: Three allmap tables have repeated owner-local consumers: four pairs of neighbor offsets, four word-sized direction selectors and a four-by-four signed-halfword arrangement table copied with an explicit sizeof bound. These tables and the following Doorinfo and Pusha task names form the same complete 0x6A-byte readonly suffix in all regions. Ordinary const definitions preserve the original bytes, object bounds and code relocations. The preceding coordinate span and earlier four task names now complete the same native readonly owner as described in allmap_readonly_geometry.
provenance.status_readonly_prefix_owner: Twelve status UI names and their directly consumed cursor positions, eight-entry StatusFriendTable, and two EU language-count arrays form one complete native readonly prefix. The tab navigation bounds select positions 0..3; the friend helper copies the complete existing record and traverses entries 0..7; EU localized resource calls select five language counts. Ordinary const definitions reproduce every original object address and the interleaved compiler alignment. The later Boogie records and name retain their existing boundaries, while descriptor data, code bodies, RAM, and encoded asset payloads are unchanged.
provenance.boss_tm_movement: Canonical 32-byte body and foot step types are preserved field-for-field. task_bos_tm_1 wraps idle phase0..7 and walking phase0..9; func_080B83C4 wraps body angle index0..10. task_bos_tm_body_1 and task_bos_tm_foot_1 explicitly select translated step indices0..15 or0..8. Reaction paths explicitly use step0..2. Foot phase bytes produce height selectors0..4. Body effect choice uses GetRandom()%4. Seven unused complete zero terminator records and four unused halfword suffix values remain separately named neutral scalar objects; no runtime access is claimed. All record/scalar bytes agree across US/JP/EU.
provenance.boss_tm_native_owner: The Trickmaster parent lifecycle owns four task pointers and a TaskPool and directly creates its body, foot, club, arm and table callbacks. These callbacks and their repeatedly consumed movement tables form one contiguous original code and initialized-data run across all regions, previously split between the end of wlogo.c, the beginning of bos2.c and a storage-only data unit. Ordinary definitions in boss_tm.c preserve all 31 initialized objects and their relocations. The private logo pools remain in wlogo.c; its naturally 0x74-byte BSS followed by the Trickmaster section with native eight-byte alignment accounts for the former four-byte filler. No data-table extent, remaining shared state or interleaved name/asset boundary is changed.
provenance.sio_readonly_owner: The SIO modes index exactly two and three existing SioAnimDef records; their pointer fields reference the same typed animation resources used by these callbacks. Both tables are read only and have no consumers outside mode_sio.c. They interleave the six mode names in US/JP; EU omits the card-exchange table and two names, and instead has two terminated byte-encoded Deck labels read by the Latin text loader. Ordinary const records, names and character-list byte arrays reproduce each complete original readonly group and every relocation target. The compiler aligns string initializers to four bytes but retains the natural byte alignment of array initializers, explaining the adjacent EU labels without extra bytes or section attributes. Obsolete raw metadata fragments and fixed-address aliases are removed; record bounds, label extents, code, RAM and encoded assets are preserved.
provenance.map_initialized_owner: The sixty-six original map configuration, callback, task, mode, debug-glyph and floor-name objects retain their complete 1556-byte initialized-data run across all regions. The map engine prefix now emits the first 348 bytes and the contiguous map task owner emits the following 1208 bytes with ordinary input alignment. Definitions retain their bounds, initializers and regional guards. The three fourteen-byte level-offset/event arrays remain mutable storage, an earlier reconstruction of their native initialized-data organization rather than evidence of writes. The two floor-name indexes and underscore move with their task consumers to map_tasks.c. EU localized records retain shared canonical declarations. Every original object/content contract is preserved; unrelated lower-ROM placements remain unchanged.
provenance.allmap_readonly_geometry: The original 32-byte coordinate span is reconstructed as two const signed-halfword tables of four x/y pairs. func_080D484C indexes the first four-pair rectangle while drawing the four door overlays. The next four pairs form a complete centered 32-pixel square in every original ROM, followed by this same owner's four-direction offset and direction-selection tables. History c4bf64c6 declared only an unsized array, so no prior C extent establishes an eight-entry array. The second four-pair table retains the address-style name gUnk_096FDC20. Assigning this dormant but geometrically complete table to the same owner is an explicit source-organization inference; no live use or uniquely recovered original array boundary is claimed. Original ROM scans find no direct pointer to any byte of the second table. Ordinary definitions place the four earlier names, both coordinate tables and the existing readonly suffix in one 218-byte section. All original bytes, existing object extents, code, relocations and RAM are unchanged, and the former absolute coordinate alias and raw data fragment are removed.
provenance.boogie_boundary: The status UI functions end at StockMesDisp. The following ten Boogie lifecycle/helper functions, private work pointer, name and descriptor share boss_boogie.c. The final three formerly status-owned helpers operate only on BoogieDiceWork and now precede its callbacks in bos4.c. Their parent pointer is the BoogieWork passed by TaskCreate, while BoogieWork.dialog is the returned Task handle; the obsolete overlapping prefix-view type is removed. The original caller uses an unsigned switch for GetBoogieDiceState, supporting one canonical u32 return contract. Fresh sequential links of ordinary text/data/BSS preserve all three original regional layouts without extra alignment or padding. The intervening raw readonly table provider remains separate; this bounded source model does not claim its ownership is recovered.
provenance.event_message_readonly: The seven task names interleave scalar-only rendering tables used by event_message.c and card.c message rendering. The active C8C glyph table is exactly two halfwords: its reader copies four bytes and toggles index zero/one. The adjacent C90 four-halfword table is a bounded reconstruction assumption: four repeated 0x0800 values, compatible with neighboring four-position tables, and no aligned original-ROM pointer to any of its eight bytes in US, JP or EU. It is retained as a separate dormant object, without claiming a live use or uniquely proven original declaration. Shared table declarations are canonical const views in msg_api.h. Ordinary definitions reproduce the complete 217-byte readonly run and its original object order in every region.
provenance.event_selector_readonly: The final count helper func_08075064 is called only by mode_eventselect_1. It and the selector directly consume the two sentinel-terminated event-ID lists, with 146 and 48 IDs respectively. The five following debug strings are used only by that selector. These objects precede the existing selector name group. Moving the unchanged helper to the beginning of mode_eventselect.c preserves sequential code in all regions; ordinary readonly definitions preserve the 600-byte data run. Its native four-byte alignment supplies the three bytes after the preceding event_message View name, without an explicit alignment directive.
provenance.darkside_initialized_owner: Eight Darkside task descriptors and seventeen map/tile-index definitions form one native 1148-byte initialized-data run in bos2.c in all three regions. The parent lifecycle creates the component tasks, every descriptor callback is defined in this owner, and its background helpers and map initializer directly consume both table groups. The storage-only bos2_background_data.c split is removed. All original types, bounds, initializers, regional asset selections and dormant pointer scalars are unchanged, including the explicit NULL initializer that AGBCC emits naturally in .data. No readonly name, Jafar data, RAM definition or source-code boundary changes. Actual background dimensions and Dsd state selectors retain the existing table-bound evidence; the separate suffix pointer scalars retain their original neutral representation and independently used asset targets. task_bos_dsd_map_0 passes exactly two by two map blocks, and every nonblank map target is a complete 32 by 32 u16 tilemap. Raw asset payloads remain untouched.
provenance.wlogo_readonly_prefix: The first seventeen Wlogo task names interleave three motion-configuration tables whose existing canonical structs are preserved. Hwt explicitly creates objects numbered zero through five; its pre-existing six-record motion-row stride fixes a six by six table, including the real zero and inactive command slots. Each live row terminates on its existing flag, and the initialization table contains the six matching object records. The Nvl motion sequence contains four records ending at the independently referenced task_wlogo_nvl_mov name. Its fourth record carries the stopping flag, but the callback still increments its index and performs the existing post-terminal field loads from the following bytes before later frames skip that branch. The four-record extent follows the next independent name, not a maximum runtime-read bound; the name is not absorbed or relabeled as a fifth record, and all existing loads remain byte-identical. All three table starts were existing fixed-address aliases; their independently bounded records meet the next table or task name exactly, and every byte agrees across US, JP and EU. Only Wlogo callbacks read their scalar fields; ordinary const definitions with private forward declarations reconstruct one native 1363-byte readonly prefix. Compiler alignment supplies the two former one-byte zero prefixes. The later Pooh motion span and six remaining task names keep their original raw/explicit placements because its additional zero records are not established by these readers. No new type, record extent, code boundary or asset payload is inferred.
provenance.boss_tm_native_readonly: The six task names, one EmyKind record, 28 bounded arm-animation arrays, and one segment-length table belong to the existing boss_tm.c owner. func_080B8334 passes the 16-byte record to the established EmyKind reader. The distinct func_080BB43C pointer/count arguments partition exactly 120 existing 20-byte TmAnimFrame records with no gaps; func_080BB5E8 uses the stored count to wrap the frame index. The former EmyKind-address-plus-offset expressions are replaced by those actual array definitions. The frame and segment-length bytes are identical in US, JP, and EU. All six nonzero halfwords after the last animation and before the independently referenced arm task name are retained as a six-element segment-length table; this capacity is an inference from the full typed span, while actual joint initialization proves only indices 0, 2, and 4. Const records and their const reader views are an explicit reconstruction supported by read-only use and the original lower-ROM group. Ordinary definitions emit the complete 2528-byte native readonly run including natural string alignment; no explicit section, alignment, filler, or asset payload changes are used. All prior name contracts remain, and new real-object contracts replace four obsolete address aliases and the two raw providers.
